article.title: VMware vCenter zero-day exploited for months before patch (CVE-2026-123890)
article.summary: A suspected China-nexus espionage group tracked as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221) has been exploiting a VMware vCenter zero-day since at least early September, more than two months before Broadcom released a fix, Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) revealed. The vulnerability (CVE-2026-123890) carries a CVSS score of 9.8 and allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to obtain an administrator session on vCenter Server, which organizations use to manage their VMware servers and virtual machines. Broadcom fixed it … More → The post VMware vCenter zero-day exploited for months before patch (CVE-2026-123890) appeared first on Help Net Security .

items.relevance_reason: Nhóm tấn công mạng liên quan đến Trung Quốc đã khai thác lỗ hổng zero-day trong VMware vCenter suốt nhiều tháng trước khi có bản vá.

article.title: Amazon: China-Linked Hackers’ AI Agents Exploited Medical Software Zero-Day
article.summary: A threat actor used autonomous Cairn AI agents to discover and exploit a critical MONAI Label vulnerability. The post Amazon: China-Linked Hackers’ AI Agents Exploited Medical Software Zero-Day appeared first on SecurityWeek .

article.title: Linux KVM Flaw CVE-2026-99312 Lets Guest VMs Access Host Memory on AMD Hosts
article.summary: A flaw in KVM, the hypervisor built into the Linux kernel, let researchers read about 127 GB of a cloud server's memory from inside a virtual machine of their own on DigitalOcean. On a shared server, that memory can include other customers' virtual machines. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-99312, affects only hosts with AMD processors and nested virtualization enabled. article.title: Ruby Patches Ruby2Shell Vulnerability That Could Lead to RCE
article.summary: Tracked as CVE-2026-132825, the bug is a heap-based buffer overflow that could lead to remote code execution (RCE). The post Ruby Patches Ruby2Shell Vulnerability That Could Lead to RCE appeared first on SecurityWeek .
